summary: this would be an space game trying to help the people to experience what goes on in the operations of an actual nasa space program
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

NASA Mission Control: Gateway Alpha is an interactive 2D space systems engineering and station walk-around simulation game. Instead of navigating sterile spreadsheets, players take on the role of an astronaut and flight director living aboard an orbital research station (Gateway Alpha).

  • Embodied Exploration: Players walk through a 5-room space station using 8-directional movement (WASD / Arrow keys) with character step-bobbing and proximity-based interaction prompts ([E] ACCESS CONSOLE).
  • Interactive Mission Decks:
    1. 🚀 Command Bridge & Flight Desk (0, -60): Accesses the Mission Design Studio, where players configure spacecraft bus structures, instruments, propulsion, orbits, and launch vehicles while managing real-time SWaP-C (Size, Weight, Power, and Cost) trade-offs.
    2. 🧪 Botanical & Exobiology Lab (-600, 0): Features apothecary specimen benches to analyze extraterrestrial crystals and catalog research science points.
    3. 📻 Capcom & Telecoms Deck (600, 0): Downlinks telemetry to NASA’s Deep Space Network (DSN) Goldstone station, triggering authentic Quindar radio beeps and flight status updates.
    4. ⚡ Boiler & Power Bay (0, 420): Manages the station's energy balance, solar array tracking angles, and reserve battery states-of-charge.
    5. 🌌 Cupola Observation Bay (0, -380): Features a velvet bench overlooking a panoramic view of Earth and space, with smooth camera zooming to observe celestial horizons.
  • Flight Operations & Mission Progression: Players design and execute multi-tier missions (Artemis I, Artemis II, and Mars Odyssey) featuring automated T-minus 10s countdowns, orbital insertion, and deep-space hazard navigation.
  • Grand Victory Ceremony: Successfully managing all station operations and mission tiers unlocks an official NASA Grand Commendation Certificate granting the player the rank of Master Flight Director with S-Rank Gold Astronaut Wings.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Bridges Theory and Practice: Aerospace engineering trade-offs often remain abstract in textbooks. This project demonstrates how a single design change—such as adding a high-resolution spectrometer—has ripple effects across mass, power demand, launch vehicle sizing, and mission budget.
  • Dual-Tier Accessibility:
    • Beginners & Students: Enjoy an approachable, cozy walk-around game where they can explore, tend plants, and launch rockets.
    • Aspiring Engineers: Can experiment with authentic mathematical constraints (payload mass margins, power balances, and orbital parameters).
  • Immediate, Frictionless Access: Available both as a native desktop game in Godot Engine 4 and as a zero-install HTML5 web simulation that runs on any PC, Mac, or tablet browser.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Inspiring STEM / STEAM Careers: Sparks interest in space exploration, aerospace engineering, astrophysics, and computer science among students of all backgrounds.
  • Teaching Systems-Thinking: Instills the core engineering principle that there is rarely a single "perfect" solution; real mission design requires balance, compromise, and collaboration.
  • Team Collaboration: Enables cooperative problem-solving where up to 4 participants can specialize in roles such as Flight Director, Systems Lead, Capcom Operator, and Science Specialist.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Game Engine: Godot Engine 4.7.2 (Node hierarchy, 2D physics layers, Area2D collision triggers, dynamic Camera2D lerp smoothing, and CanvasLayer HUD).
  • Primary Code: GDScript (Godot 4's high-performance, object-oriented language utilizing custom classes, signal-slot architecture, and typed variables).
  • Web Engine: HTML5 Canvas, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+) for the zero-dependency browser simulation.
  • Graphics & Art: SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) for crisp, resolution-independent pixel art (the chibi astronaut, wooden CRT consoles, spacecraft, and celestial bodies).
  • Procedural Sound Synthesis: Custom in-engine 16-bit sound synthesizer in both GDScript (AudioStreamWAV) and JavaScript (Web Audio API), generating authentic 2525 Hz / 2475 Hz NASA Quindar radio beeps, thruster pulses, and chimes directly in memory with zero external sound files.
  • Target Hardware: Standard cross-platform consumer laptops and desktops (no high-end GPU required).

5. How is your project creative?

  • The "Stardew Valley in Space" Aesthetic:
    • Rather than relying on cold, intimidating neon-cyan sci-fi interfaces, the project reimagines the station as a warm, cozy orbital sanctuary. It features staggered oak timber floors, crimson Persian rugs with gold tassels, brass wall lanterns, terracotta potted ferns, and an antique vacuum-tube radio cabinet.
    • This aesthetic reduces cognitive fatigue and makes space systems engineering feel welcoming, tactile, and human.
  • Embodied Interaction:
    • Instead of navigating static spreadsheets, the player physically walks their astronaut to dedicated stations, grounding technical engineering decisions in an interactive living space.
  • 100% Code-Generated Procedural Worlds:
    • Starfields, twinkling brightness animations, floorboard seams, and sound waves are generated procedurally at runtime, keeping the entire project footprint under 100 KB with instant load times.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  1. Engineering Fidelity vs. Educational Flow (SWaP-C Constraints):
    • Mass Margin (MLV≥Mdry+MpropM_{LV} \ge M_{dry} + M_{prop}MLV​≥Mdry​+Mprop​): Enforcing strict launch vehicle lift capacities.
    • Power Balance (Pgen≥Pbus+PpayloadP_{gen} \ge P_{bus} + P_{payload}Pgen​≥Pbus​+Ppayload​): Modeling solar panel generation against instrument power consumption.
    • Budget & Comms Caps: Balancing scientific return against project cost and Deep Space Network downlink bandwidth.
  2. User Experience (UX) & Ergonomics:
    • Dynamic interaction pills ([E] ACCESS DESK), color-coded telemetry badges (green for nominal, amber for warning), and camera damping to ensure fluid gameplay.
  3. Cross-Platform Deployability:
    • Ensuring the project works as both a clean, single-click Windows .exe export and a zero-install web application.
  4. Human Factors in Spaceflight:
    • Incorporating restorative environments (like the Cupola viewing bay and warm hearth lighting) to reflect the real-world psychological needs of astronauts during long-duration space expeditions.
